decisions.reason: The single-board architecture makes the existing power-board connection condition and main-board Schottky location labels obsolete while preserving the DCDC1 rail function.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: I was thinking, if you have time for a new project and are willing to do it, that we try to make as cheap as possible single board for this project. So everything will be on one board and from start we try to match JLCPCB Basica component (as much as possible). It will have much less connectors as there are no interboard connectors. Also if you have some idea on how to make something better/cheaper but have same functionality you can suggest. I can add it as new milestone to this project and we can agree on price. What do you think does it make sense?

value_updates.voltage_compensation_purpose: Compensate for the integrated-board Schottky diode drop so the system rail remains at 3.3V under all conditions

decisions.reason: The requirement already describes the functional battery and system power path without depending on separate-board or interboard-connector semantics.
Integrating the boards does not determine a different battery connector family, pin count, pin functions, or unresolved pin order.
The AXP2101 exposed-pad heat-transfer requirement remains valid unchanged on the integrated board.
The source preserves functionality and does not change the LED part, supply voltage, GPIO, power control, or data-level interface.
The existing message-750 MODIFY already records elimination of interboard connectors, removes their obsolete orientation, and moves the requirement scope to the integrated board.

The old activation condition depends on connecting USB-C without the power board, which is impossible after integration, but the source does not specify the replacement source-selection or standalone-mode trigger.
